text:
ana: Quick q — staging logs are showing Referer URLs that sometimes include user emails in query params (example: /invite?email=foo@example.com). Can we keep Referer header for debugging or should we strip it? cc @yuki

yuki: Short answer: don't log PII in plaintext. If Referer can contain emails or tokens, we should not store the full header. Log domain+path only, strip querystring or scrub sensitive params.

sam: If we need query params for debugging, one pattern is HMAC the param values with a service key and log hmac(value). That gives a stable pseudonym you can search for without storing the raw value. Access to rehydrate should be gated.

mike: Also seeing Cookie header captured in some proxy logs for routing. Are cookie/session ids allowed to be logged (pseudonymized) for debugging?

yuki: Cookie values are sensitive. DO NOT log raw session ids or auth tokens. Options: 1) drop Cookie header entirely from logs; 2) replace value with a deterministic pseudonym (e.g., hmac(session_id)[:8]) + "..."; 3) if you must capture a full value for an active incident, follow the temporary-access flow (ticket + approval). For Authorization/Bearer: drop entirely.

ana: (typo) — sorry, meant ana: Got it. For Referer scrub, is a simple regex that removes email-like query params OK? e.g. 

```
# pseudo
referer = re.sub(r"([?&]email=)[^&]+", r"\1<redacted>", referer)
referer = referer.split('?')[0]  # or keep scrubbed query if needed
```

yuki: That regex is fine as a stopgap. Prefer a small whitelist for debugging params we allow to persist (e.g., utm_*, campaign_id) and scrub other params by default. If you want to keep a param value for debugging, HMAC it server-side and log only the digest.

security-bot: Policy excerpt: "PII in logs is prohibited. Strip/query-scrub Referer and remove auth tokens. Temporary exceptions require approval from sec oncall and a ticket." https://redwood.company/policies/logging-pii 

sam: Also note: for Dedicated/Private customers, config may differ — deploy defaults should still scrub, but customers can request an opt-in export with contractual controls.

ana: (again) ana: OK thanks all — I'll open a tiny PR on the proxy to: 1) drop Authorization, 2) strip query params from Referer unless whitelisted, 3) mask Cookie values to first8+..., and 4) add a link to the temp-access runbook in logs. Will tag @yuki for review and include the ticket if we need raw values. :thumbsup:

yuki: Sounds good. If you need a quick regex whitelist or the HMAC helper function, ping me and I'll paste the snippet.

mike: Thanks — will check existing proxy dashboards to ensure we're not capturing anything else.

(reacts: ana :thumbsup:, sam :eyes:)
